Here we introduce compression of corrugated elastic sheets to experimentally observe and manipulate these bits, their interactions, and their pathways. We apply spatial gradients at the boundaries as a general technique to control the pathways. Besides mechanical memory, where the sheet remembers earlier extremal driving, we observe a pathway where interactions between material bits produce an elementary computation: counting to two. Our work paves the way for controlling material bits in other systems and suggests a tight link between computations and the complex response of frustrated
